backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Within fit_predict, split the training molecules into an inner train and validation part using a GroupKFold on Murcko scaffold strings (hold out about 20 percent of scaffolds, seeded). Fit CatBoost MAE with eval_set on the inner validation residuals, use_best_model=True, early_stopping_rounds=100 and up to 2000 iterations. Then refit on all training molecules using the best iteration count found, scaled by 1.1, with the same seed. This tunes the iteration count on scaffold-held-out data rather than fixing it at 800.
backlog.title: Scaffold-grouped early stopping inside the residual fit

backlog.spec: Train CatBoost with 1200 iterations. Then average the predictions made at 600, 900 and 1200 trees using model.predict(X, ntree_end=k) for each k. This is snapshot averaging along the boosting path. Add the OLS prior as before.
backlog.title: Target-noise snapshot averaging

backlog.spec: Keep the incumbent pipeline and add a single post-processing line: after computing the final predictions (CatBoost residual plus OLS prior), clip them with np.clip(pred, y.min(), y.max()) where y is the training target array of the current fold, and return the clipped values. Caco-2 log-permeability values span a bounded range, and the additive OLS-plus-boosting form can extrapolate past the training extremes on unusual scaffolds; clipping costs nothing and can only change the few most extreme predictions. No other change.
backlog.title: Clip predictions to the observed training range

backlog.spec: Inside fit_predict, replace the fixed 800 iterations with early stopping on a scaffold-disjoint inner split. Compute Murcko scaffolds for the training molecules with rdkit.Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, group rows by scaffold, and use a seeded shuffle of the distinct scaffolds to hold out whole scaffolds covering about 20 percent of the rows as an eval set. Fit the CatBoost MAE model on the remaining rows with iterations=3000, od_type='Iter', early_stopping_rounds=100 and eval_set=(X_val, resid_val), then predict the test molecules with the best iteration. The OLS prior is still fit on all training rows and added back unchanged. This lets each fold choose its own boosting length against unseen skeletons rather than inheriting a global constant.
backlog.title: Scaffold-held-out early stopping for the residual boosting

backlog.spec: Replace the single CatBoost fit on the OLS residual with an average over 5 CatBoost MAE models that differ only in their random seed (random_seed = seed*100 + i for i in range(5)), keeping depth, learning rate and iterations as they are. Average the 5 residual predictions before adding back the OLS prior term A_te @ coef. To keep the model stochastic enough for seed averaging to help, give each model bootstrap_type='Bernoulli' with subsample=0.8 so the seeds actually produce different trees. This is pure variance reduction on the component the notes identify as the remaining noise source, and it is the second explicitly suggested next step. Use thread_count=8 and verbose=0 as now.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged CatBoost residual model

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and the CatBoost MAE residual model. In featurize, drop the 2048 Morgan count block and feed only the RDKit Descriptors.descList values (nan_to_num as before) to CatBoost. Morgan bits were only ever tested as additions or replacements alongside descriptors, and the notes show the fingerprint block dominates the feature count. This ablation tests whether the 200-odd descriptors alone carry the signal, and so whether the fingerprint block is adding noise on this small dataset.
backlog.title: Descriptor-only residual model without Morgan bits

backlog.spec: Keep the incumbent OLS prior and residual setup, but replace the single CatBoost fit with an average over 5 models that differ only in random seed: for i in range(5), fit a CatBoostRegressor with random_seed=seed*1000+i (same depth, learning_rate, iterations, MAE loss, thread_count=8) on the identical residual target and feature matrix, then average the 5 predicted residuals before adding back the OLS prediction A_te @ coef. Compute the train and test feature matrices once and reuse them across the 5 fits so the cost is only the boosting. Mean-of-seeds removes the stochastic part of CatBoost's variance at no bias cost; if runtime is a concern, drop to 3 seeds.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged residual CatBoost

backlog.spec: Keep the incumbent OLS-prior-plus-residual pipeline and change only the tree shape: pass grow_policy='Lossguide', max_leaves=24 and depth=8 (Lossguide requires depth as an upper bound) to the CatBoostRegressor, keeping loss_function='MAE', learning_rate=0.05, iterations=800, random_seed=seed, verbose=0 and thread_count=8. Lossguide grows leaf-wise toward the largest loss reduction instead of building symmetric depth-6 trees, so the model can spend splits on the few informative fingerprint bits rather than splitting every level uniformly. If CatBoost rejects any argument combination, keep max_leaves=24 and drop the explicit depth. No feature or target changes.
backlog.title: CatBoost Lossguide grow policy on the residual

backlog.spec: After computing final predictions in fit_predict, clip them with np.clip to the [min, max] of train_y, or to the 1st and 99th percentiles of train_y. Change nothing else.
backlog.title: Clip predictions to training range

backlog.spec: Before featurisation and base_features, preprocess each SMILES. Use rdMolStandardize.LargestFragmentChooser to keep the largest fragment, then rdMolStandardize.Uncharger to neutralise it. Fall back to the original molecule on any exception. Apply this to both train and test molecules via a shared helper that returns the mol.
backlog.title: Salt stripping and neutralisation

backlog.spec: Keep the pipeline unchanged and only regularise the CatBoost residual model more heavily: pass l2_leaf_reg=12.0 (default is 3.0) and raise ITERS to 1600 while keeping DEPTH=6 and LR=0.05. With a 728-row training fold and a wide sparse feature block, stronger leaf shrinkage lets the model take more small, better-regularised steps. Do not add subsampling or column sampling (slot 22 showed those hurt); change only l2_leaf_reg and iterations. Keep loss_function='MAE', random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8.
backlog.title: Stronger leaf regularisation with a longer path

backlog.spec: Keep the pipeline unchanged and switch the residual CatBoost model from its default symmetric trees to grow_policy='Lossguide' with max_leaves=24, depth=8 (depth acts as a cap under Lossguide), LR=0.04 and ITERS=1500. Symmetric trees spend splits uniformly, which is wasteful on a feature block where a handful of descriptors carry most of the signal and 2048 fingerprint bins are mostly empty; leaf-wise growth concentrates capacity on the informative regions. This stays inside the CatBoost MAE family that already won, so it is a growth-policy change rather than a model-family swap. Keep loss_function='MAE', random_seed=seed, verbose=0, thread_count=8.
backlog.title: CatBoost Lossguide grow policy on the residual

backlog.spec: Extend the linear prior features with a few more physically motivated terms: NumHAcceptors, NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3 and aromatic ring count. Fit with Ridge(alpha=3) on standardised features instead of OLS on 4 terms. CatBoost then fits the residual as before.
backlog.title: Crippen atom-contribution linear prior

backlog.spec: Keep train.py exactly as it is (OLS prior on TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP, CatBoost MAE on the residual, Morgan counts plus RDKit descriptors) and change only the tree depth: set DEPTH = 4 instead of 6. With 728 molecules and ~2250 features, depth 6 trees have 64 leaves and likely overfit scaffold-disjoint folds; depth 4 gives 16 leaves and a smoother residual fit. Change nothing else, so the result is a clean one-knob read on tree capacity. If this is clearly better than the incumbent, the same knob can later be pushed to depth 3.
backlog.title: Shallower CatBoost trees on the residual

backlog.spec: Replace the single four-term OLS prior with the equal-weight average of three small OLS priors fit on disjoint descriptor subsets: (a) TPSA and NumHDonors, (b) MolLogP and MolWt, (c) NumRotatableBonds, FractionCSP3 and NumHAcceptors. Each prior is a least-squares fit with an intercept on the training fold via np.linalg.lstsq; the combined prior prediction is the mean of the three fitted values, for both train (to form the residual target) and test (to add back). Everything downstream is unchanged: CatBoost MAE on the residual with the existing features and hyperparameters. Averaging low-dimensional priors reduces the variance of the linear stage and spreads it over complementary physicochemical axes rather than relying on one four-term fit.
backlog.title: Average several small linear priors instead of one OLS

backlog.spec: Take the two-phase residual schedule that scored best so far (a 400-iteration CatBoost with loss_function='Huber:delta=0.3' fit on the OLS residual, then a second CatBoost MAE model fit on what the first phase leaves over, summing both phase predictions on top of the OLS prior) and wrap the whole two-phase procedure in a 3-member seed average: run it for random_seed = seed, seed+1, seed+2 with bootstrap_type='Bernoulli', subsample=0.8, and average the three final predictions. The single-run version measured 0.3701 against an incumbent of 0.3711, which is inside the 0.0037 noise band, so this both averages away the per-seed noise and re-measures the best candidate at the same time.
backlog.title: Seed-averaged two-phase Huber-then-MAE boosting

backlog.spec: Keep the incumbent structure and retune only the boosting step size and length: set LR = 0.02 and ITERS = 2500 (instead of LR = 0.05, ITERS = 800), leaving depth, loss function, features and the OLS prior untouched. The total shrinkage budget is similar but each tree commits less, which usually helps MAE boosting on small noisy regression sets. Check the runtime stays within the 10-minute, 15-fit budget; the current job is far under the limit, but if 2500 iterations at depth 6 is too slow, reduce to ITERS = 2000 rather than changing anything else.
backlog.title: Slow learning rate with more iterations

backlog.spec: Keep the OLS prior and residual target. Train CatBoost MAE in three equal stages of 300 iterations each using CatBoost's init_model warm start (or by refitting with a smaller learning rate per stage if warm start is awkward): stage learning rates 0.08, 0.04, 0.02 applied by cosine decay across the total of 900 iterations. Keep depth 6, MAE loss and seed unchanged. A decaying step size at the end of boosting can settle the MAE leaf values more finely than a constant rate of 0.05.
backlog.title: Cosine decay of the boosting learning rate

backlog.spec: Compute 5-fold out-of-fold CatBoost predictions (300 iterations) on the training set. Drop the 5% of training rows with the largest absolute OOF residual. Then fit the final CatBoost MAE model on the remaining rows, with the OLS prior refit on them too.
backlog.title: Out-of-fold residual trimming

memo: Helped: compact descriptors (MACCS 0.4096 vs 0.4417 baseline), CatBoost MAE loss (0.3837), and an OLS prior on TPSA/MolWt/NumHDonors/MolLogP with CatBoost fit on residuals (0.3757 and 0.3664; incumbent mean_adjusted 0.3711). Did not help: Morgan counts (0.4451), Tanimoto kernel ridge (0.4357), MLP (0.4734), LightGBM l1 (0.3882), stacking (0.3904), PCA (0.3893), torsion counts (0.3771), 3D shape (0.3780), ElasticNet (0.3840), monotone constraints (0.3869), ionisation SMARTS (0.3764), local linear prior (0.3886), Nystroem prior (0.3915). Within noise (sd about 0.0037): residual refinements (0.3718, 0.3716), scaffold weighting (0.3724), median prior (0.3726), pruning (0.3728). Best recent: two-phase Huber then MAE boosting (0.3701), only -0.0010 vs incumbent, so likely noise. Plateau: extra features, model swaps and target tricks lose. Next: tune CatBoost depth, learning rate, iterations and l2 on the residual setup, which is untried, and seed-average CatBoost. Replicate anything near 0.37. Avoid family swaps and feature stacking.
